subject: Capacity surge playbook & burst policy for Omega Media Dedicated
messages:
From: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@omegamedia.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben.turner@omegamedia.com
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial sizing questions for Dedicated

Jonas — thanks for the call earlier. To recap, Omega's peak events drive short, steep bursts: 100k concurrent inference requests across our personalization pipeline for 8–12 minutes, mid-month and end-of-quarter. We need guidance on how Dedicated would handle those bursts without paying for steady-state reserved GPUs at peak.

Attached is a rough QPS/time profile and our current batch latency SLOs. Two asks: 
1) ballpark capacity that can cover the 100k spike with <300ms p99 for our shorter prompts, and
2) recommended autoscaling/burst policy so we don't have to commit to 10x baseline capacity.

Can you share a playbook or example configs you use for other media customers?

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Cho
Head of ML Platform, Omega Media

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@omegamedia.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial sizing questions for Dedicated

Alyssa — great summary, thanks. I attached a short "surge playbook" and a starter worksheet. High-level thoughts:
- For 100k concurrent short requests, sequence length matters — if median tokens < 64 we can push higher effective throughput per GPU.
- Typical approach: reserve baseline for predictable steady-state (we recommend baseline for 75–80% of average daily QPS) and add burst nodes via an autoscale group with a short warm-up path (pre-warmed caches + fast-attach policy).
- We commonly recommend a hybrid of reserved + on-demand burst for media customers to avoid 10x steady-state cost.

I'm looping in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (solutions) to sketch concrete numbers. I'm also including the MOP (managed operations playbook) for SLA/credits during burst events.

Next step: can you confirm the median request size and your target p99 token latency? Once we have that Karthik will draft an instance/GPU mix and an autoscale policy (min/max/burst ratio).

Attachment: omega_capacity_estimate_v3.xlsx

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@omegamedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial sizing questions for Dedicated

Alyssa — quick technical note from infra: we want to avoid cold-starting full GPU instances during a spike. Proposed pattern:
1) baseline fleet: N x A100-80GB (or equivalent quantized nodes) sized to handle 60–75% of average daily traffic; these are the reserved capacity.
2) warm pool: a small set of pre-initialized containers on kept-warm GPUs (smaller instance type or fractionally provisioned GPUs if your support vendor allows) to absorb the first wave and populate KV caches. Typical warm pool size = 5–10% of the estimated peak.
3) burst autoscale group: scale to full-size GPU nodes when metrics (queue length, p95 latency) cross thresholds; scale-in with hysteresis after sustained drop.

I'll draft a numeric example if you confirm median tokens and model variant. Also attaching a GPU-mapping diagram we use for planning.

--Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: roster_gpu_mapping.png

Also, we run regionally in us-east + us-west; can you recommend scaling across regions vs centralizing bursts in one region?

Alyssa

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@omegamedia.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial sizing questions for Dedicated

Hi Alyssa — re: contract terms and overage: we typically offer two options for Dedicated customers with predictable burst patterns:
1) capped overage with negotiated unit price and monthly true-up (recommended for cost predictability), or
2) burst credits pool: pre-purchased credits you draw down during events; unused credits roll-forward for one quarter.

For SLA: we can offer an "event SLA" for booked burst windows (we pre-warm capacity and treat it as scheduled reserved capacity) — that's documented in the MOP term sheet. For unscheduled bursts, we provide best-effort autoscale with fallback to a slightly lower-tier model variant and offer partial uptime credits if p99 latency targets are missed.

On regions: if your traffic splits across coasts during events, it's best to have regional warm pools to avoid cross-region egress and latency hits. If most spikes originate in a single region, centralizing is acceptable and more cost-efficient.

I've attached the MOP term sheet and included sample language for burst credits and overage caps.

Attachment: mop_sla_term_sheet.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Alyssa / Ben — thanks for the details. Action items and proposal: 
- We'll produce a numeric sizing workbook by Tue (estimate N=6 A100-80GB reserved + warm pool 1 GPU-equivalent per 10 peak nodes + burst cap up to 20 additional nodes across us-east/us-west). See attached worksheet for full math.
- Commercial options: (a) capped overage at $X/token for bursts above committed capacity, (b) 3-month burst credit bundle at a 12% discount. Marissa will own the term-sheet edits.
- Operational play: schedule pre-warm windows for predictable events (we recommend 30–60 minutes pre-warm), and enable autoscale thresholds tied to queue length and p95 latency. Karthik will template the Kubernetes/daemonset warm-pool config we use.

Can you confirm preferred option for pricing (capped overage vs credit bundle) and whether we should plan regional warm pools? If you want, we can lock in a short technical workshop next week to walk your infra team through the warm-pool and cache priming steps.

Best — Jonas
